Most questions in stream ecology can be attacked from more than one direction,
and the directions disagree in instructive ways. A whole reach integrates
everything happening in it but hides who did what; a chamber isolates one
patch of streambed but changes the flow over it. I use both, and the same
applies to nutrients, where a pulse and a steady drip answer different
questions about the same biofilm.

## Ecosystem metabolism

![A benthic chamber before deployment: transparent walls, internal circulation and a logging probe.](images/methods/chamber-closeup.jpg){.side-figure}

**Open-channel.** A multiparameter sonde logs dissolved oxygen, temperature,
pH and conductivity every few minutes for several days. Photosynthesis,
respiration and gas exchange with the atmosphere are then separated from the
shape of the daily oxygen curve. The estimate covers the whole reach,
including the hyporheic zone and patches nobody would think to sample, which
is its strength; its weakness is that reaeration must be estimated well or the
biology is swamped by it.

**Benthic chambers.** Sealed transparent chambers enclose a known area of
streambed, with light and dark incubations giving net production and
respiration separately, and on substrates chosen on purpose: travertine crust,
loose cobble, sand, macrophyte. A chamber answers *which patch does what*,
which the reach-scale estimate cannot, at the cost of altering flow and
turbulence inside it.

![Chamber arrays incubating on the streambed, paired light and dark.](images/methods/chamber-array.jpg){.side-figure-left}

Running both in the same reach is the useful part. When the sum of the patches
matches the open-channel estimate, the budget closes; when it does not, the
difference is itself a result, pointing to a compartment that was not sampled
or to gas exchange being off.

## Nutrient uptake

![Setting up the downstream station before a pulse addition.](images/methods/slug-station.jpg){.side-figure}

**Pulse (slug) additions.** A single release of a conservative tracer together
with nutrient, sampled intensively downstream. Fast, cheap, and tolerant of
remote sites with no power. The reach sees a transient pulse of concentration
well above ambient, so what is measured is uptake under enrichment, not at
background.

**Constant-rate (drip) additions.** Tracer and nutrient dripped at a steady
rate until the reach reaches a plateau. This holds the enrichment constant
while the biofilm equilibrates, which makes the uptake estimate cleaner and
lets several enrichment levels be compared to describe the saturation curve.
It costs hours of pumping, carboys of solution and a team.

![Incubation trays in the streambed during an addition.](images/methods/incubation-tray.jpg){.side-figure-left}

Both are paired with water chemistry: filtered aliquots for ammonium, nitrate,
soluble reactive phosphorus, alkalinity and calcium, preserved in the field and
kept cold until analysis.

## Consumers

![Excretion incubation: a fish held in a bag of filtered stream water while nutrients accumulate.](images/methods/excretion-bag.jpg){.side-figure}

**Excretion assays.** Individual animals are held briefly in a known volume of
filtered stream water; the nutrients that accumulate give per-individual
excretion rates of nitrogen and phosphorus, and the N:P ratio of what they
release. Body mass and taxon are recorded, because both govern the rate.

**Community density and biomass.** Excretion per individual becomes an
ecosystem flux only when multiplied by how many individuals are there. Fish
assemblages are surveyed by seining and by underwater counts along fixed
transects; molluscs and other benthic consumers are counted and measured in
quadrats. Aggregations are mapped rather than averaged away, since that is
where the biogeochemical hotspots are.

![Seining a reach to estimate fish density and biomass.](images/methods/seine-net.jpg){.side-figure-left}

![Measuring bivalves for biomass and excretion scaling.](images/methods/mollusc-measure.jpg){.side-figure}

Scaling the two together turns a physiological measurement into a term in the
nutrient budget of the reach, which is what makes consumer-driven recycling
comparable with uptake by the streambed.

## Water chemistry and habitat

![Water sampling and field measurements along a reach.](images/methods/water-sampling.jpg){.side-figure-left}

Discharge by dilution gauging or velocity-area, reach geometry, canopy cover
and substrate composition, alkalinity and calcium for the carbonate system,
and nutrient aliquots filtered and preserved on site. None of this is glamorous
and all of it decides whether the rest of the numbers mean anything.

## Biomonitoring

In consultancy work the same toolkit is used under a different contract:
phytoplankton and zooplankton, benthic macroinvertebrates, fish assemblages
and water quality, sampled under QA/QC and sample-traceability protocols, with
indicators computed for environmental licensing.
